tolerance.reason: CPU, FP32, one thread, deterministic algorithms; same operations in the same order as the original

recorded_differences.description: The epoch validation loss (the early-stopping and checkpoint monitor) is the mean of the per-slide -log softmax[label]. The original stacks the per-slide float32 logs and sums and divides in float32 (utils/utils.py:cross_entropy_torch, logged by models/model_interface.py:validation_epoch_end); WSIP's shared evaluator averages the per-slide float32 losses in float64 (wsip/evaluation/evaluator.py:39). The per-slide losses are identical; only the final rounding of the mean differs.
recorded_differences.reason: The aggregation lives in the shared evaluator, not in the TransMIL adapter; changing it would change CLAM's validation loss. Whether to add an opt-in float32 aggregation is a framework decision (validation_loss_aggregation).

bound.rule: the candidate's value, rounded to float32 as Lightning logs it, is at most one float32 ulp from the reference value; every selection decision (best, wait_count, should_stop, stopped_epoch, selected checkpoint) is still compared exactly

parity.limit_line: Limits: synthetic inputs, CPU only, compared with the compatibility-patched original as recorded in stage 3. Not a certification.

params.note: embed_dim 1024 because TransMIL hard-codes Linear(1024, 512); 10 bags so val and test each hold both classes; non-square bags of 122-195 rows are padded to 12x12..14x14 grids

Optimizer.lr raised to 2e-3 and General.patience lowered to 2 (both exposed by the original config) so EarlyStopping (strict val_loss improvement, no minimum epoch) fires within 12 epochs; at lr 2e-4 val_loss improves every epoch. 11 train bags give an odd accumulation tail (6 optimizer steps per epoch)

caveats.text: Compared with the original code after 9 declared compatibility patches, not with its published GPU runs.
Two synthetic CPU cases of 10 and 17 bags, 5 to 195 instances each, 1024-dimensional. No real tissue was in this comparison.
Parameters over 4,096 elements were compared per step through a 64-element sample and summary values. Initial and final weights were compared in full.
One value sits outside the 0.0: the validation-loss mean differs by 1 float32 ulp (5.96e-08). It is recorded and provisionally approved by the agent; its report status is "pending lab approval".
19 decisions along the way were answered by the agent and marked provisional. No lab member has confirmed them.
An agent wrote the comparison tests and the tool checked them with tamper runs. The independent verifier built on Oct 27 lists only clam, so it has not judged this method.

stage3: No case has more than 256 tokens, so the multi-token Nystrom landmark regime is not covered. Val and test each need at least 2 bags with both classes: the fixture puts index%5==3 in val and index%5==4 in test, and a 1-bag val split crashes the original's torchmetrics call on a 0-d squeeze. That means at least 10 bags, and the 2,000,000-element fixture limit at the hard-coded width 1024 then caps bags at 195 instances (at most 197 tokens, padded to 256 by NystromAttention).

Parameters with more than 4096 elements (_fc1.weight, to_qkv/to_out weights, PPEG conv weights) are recorded per optimizer step as a fixed 64-element strided sample plus float64 sum, sum of squares and max-abs; full per-step tensors would exceed the 50 MB evidence limit. Small parameters (biases, LayerNorms, cls_token, _fc2, res_conv) are recorded in full every step. Initial weights and the selected final weights are recorded in full.

The reference runs CPU FP32 with torch 2.11 / pytorch-lightning 1.9.5 / torchmetrics 0.7.3 / nystrom-attention 0.0.9 / einops 0.3.0 / numpy 2.2.6. It does not use the original's GPU AMP (precision 16, O2) or its torch 1.7-1.10 / Lightning 1.2.3-1.5.10 stack, so that version difference is a known deviation.

nystrom-qkv-view-clone-v1 clones the q/k/v head tensors before the library's in-place 'q *= scale', because torch 2.11 forbids in-place edits of chunk() views. Forward values are unchanged and gradients are those of the same graph, but torch 1.7's deprecated in-place-on-view autograd path was not reproduced.

Loss evidence (step/*/loss) is the training_step CrossEntropy value. Lightning's division by accumulate_grad_batches=2 before backward happens inside Lightning and is visible only through the recorded gradients. Each optimizer step lists its bags in optstep/*/bag_steps. At the end of an epoch a 1-bag tail group (11 train bags in early_stop_short_bags) is still stepped.

early_stop_short_bags uses Optimizer.lr 2e-3 and General.patience 2 (both config options of the original) so that EarlyStopping fires: it stops after epoch 4 and selects epoch 2. At the reference lr of 2e-4, val_loss improved every epoch and nothing stopped. defaults_long_bags uses the shipped defaults (lr 2e-4, wd 1e-5, patience 10, seed 2021) for 4 epochs.

data_shuffle True (random instance permutation, random.seed(count*50)) is not exercised, per the deterministic_only answer. The tensorboard and CSV loggers are not built because tensorboard is not installed, and DataLoader workers run in-process instead of 8 worker processes. Both are declared environment patches.
Test metrics (Accuracy, CohenKappa, F1, Recall, Precision, AUROC) come from 2-bag test splits and are only smoke-level values.
The pipeline's rm wrapper only deletes files, so the 14 superseded or failed debugging run folders under runs/manual could not be removed; only the two latest successful runs are current.
stage5: Inputs are small synthetic bags (5-195 rows of 1024-d random features) on CPU in FP32 with one thread. Parity with the original's GPU AMP (precision 16, O2) run, other thread counts and real Camelyon16 features is not shown.
The reference is the patched CPU run on torch 2.11 / pytorch-lightning 1.9.5 / torchmetrics 0.7.3, not the original's pinned library versions.
Only short runs are covered (4 and 5 epochs, 24 and 55 bag steps). Bags of 256 or more tokens are not covered, so the Nystrom landmark-grouping path with l > 1 is not exercised.

WSIP does not compute Cohen's kappa or macro precision (decision kappa_metric). The parity harness computes them with sklearn from the candidate's predictions, so their match shows the predictions agree, not that WSIP reports them.
WSIP never scores the test split (decision validation_only). The harness reproduces the original's test stage by applying the candidate's predict_step with the selected weights to the test bags.

Because the 1-ulp val_loss difference is bounded rather than removed, a tie between two epochs' validation losses within one float32 ulp could select a different epoch than the original. It did not happen here.
data_shuffle True, n_classes > 2, grad_acc other than 2, and resume of a mid-epoch run are not covered.
